narrations: Welcome to Episode 4, the finale of our Hello World, pg_bio intro series! Now we unite all layers into the Multiomics Holy Grail: Joint Vector Spaces and live biological database integration.

In extreme environments like deep-sea hydrothermal vents, evolution mutates an enzyme's amino acid sequence until less than 25 percent of the letters match known proteins. Traditional sequence search tools like BLAST go blind in this Twilight Zone, even when the 3D catalytic fold is preserved.

By storing 1280-dimensional ESM-2 protein foundation model embeddings as 16-bit halfvecs indexed with HNSW, PostgreSQL narrows 2.34 million dark proteins down to the top 15 structural twins in 0.4 milliseconds.

Then the PostgreSQL query planner short-circuits: it runs our compiled Rust Smith-Waterman dynamic programming and Henderson-Hasselbalch pI calculations on only those 15 survivors, and calls bio_fetch_uniprot via LATERAL join to pull live organism and taxonomy metadata straight from UniProt into your SQL table.

From 1D DNA intervals, to 3D Morton pockets, to sparse CSR graphs, to HNSW vector discovery—you now know the core multiomics stack in PostgreSQL. Dive deeper at ideia dot me and star pg_bio on GitHub!
